Available US life-table vintages

Source: R/models.R
us_lifetable_vintages.Rd

Reports the fitted-model vintages this package ships, with the provenance and race semantics needed to choose one. Vintages are **not** interchangeable — model structure differs, not only fitted values.

Usage

us_lifetable_vintages()

Value

A data frame with one row per usable vintage and columns: `vintage` (character identifier), `n_strata` (integer, always 9), `nonwhite_code` (character, the stratum code this vintage uses for its non-white category), `nonwhite_meaning` (character, what that category actually contains), `added` (character date the fits were added, where known, otherwise `NA`).

There is deliberately no `source` column: `R/` carries no literal share path. `data-raw/build-models.R` names the location the fits are restored from.

Read `nonwhite_meaning` before citing a stratum

The `table2023` non-white category is stored under code `b` but is a risk-weighted average of Black, Asian, American Indian and Hispanic death rates. It is not Black. The macro's own comment says otherwise and is wrong.

Examples

us_lifetable_vintages()
#>     vintage n_strata nonwhite_code
#> 1   table84        9             o
#> 2 table2008        9             b
#> 3 table2023        9             b
#>                                                                                                                                                                        nonwhite_meaning
#> 1                                                                                                                                 Other (all non-white), named honestly by this vintage
#> 2                                                                                                                      Black, per the macro's documentation; not independently verified
#> 3 risk-weighted average of Black, Asian, American Indian and Hispanic death rates, weighted by number at risk. NOT Black, despite the stratum code and despite the macro's own comment.
#>        added
#> 1       <NA>
#> 2       <NA>
#> 3 2025-12-23
